Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117154/assets/c4cf12ec9b53282620c1730f824c96d98e0b9dbabee0478bf258cf6c2741da81.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 1+y+z},
$$

where

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117154/assets/b497e6ef73b5b16e11baa08819e9628d3b5e1f2ee4d05fbafec48f73e087cbf1.png)

Hence, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le 1+y+z}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1+y+z}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[x]_{x=0}^{x=1+y+z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1+y+z)-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}1+y+z\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(1+y)z+\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}1+y+\frac{1}{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}+y\,dy \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}y+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2})-0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
